# dsh-plugin-ui-zoom
Whole-interface zoom for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): scale the **entire** Web UI — sidebar, menus, modal
s, icons and text — from 70% to 160%.
Built-in DSH font size only affects conversation prose. This plugin scales everything, and compensat
es the layout so zooming out shows **more text per line** instead of a narrower reading column.
## Features
- **Ctrl+wheel** zoom, 5% per notch, accumulated over trackpads so a two-finger swipe does not jump

ten steps
- **Keyboard shortcuts registered with DSH's own shortcut center** (`Mod+=` / `Mod+-` / `M

od+0` on Desktop, `Mod+Alt+…` on Web), so they appear in `Mod+/` and users can rebind them
- **Inlin

e pill** next to the composer: `− 100% +`, click the percentage to reset
- Range 70%–160%, remembere

d per origin in `localStorage` (`dsh-ui-zoom`)
- Content-width compensation: the host caps the readi

ng column at 920px, so the cap is scaled by `1 / zoom`, keeping the column's physical width stable
-
Cleans up after itself: removing the plugin restores the document and drops every listener and comm
eans up after itself: removing the plugin restores the document and drops every listener and command
## Install
Install it from the **Plugins** page in DSH (search the npm name), or:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart `dsh web` afterwards.
## Usage
| Action | Desktop | Web |

| Zoom in | `Ctrl/⌘` + wheel, `Mod+=` | `Ctrl+Alt+=` |
| Zoom out | `Ctrl/⌘` + wheel, `Mod+-` | `Ctr

l+Alt+-` |
| Reset to 100% | click the percentage, `Mod+0` | `Ctrl+Alt+0` |
`Mod` is `⌘` on macOS and `Ctrl` on Windows/Linux. All three bindings are editable in DSH's keyboard
shortcut panel (`Mod+/`); the plugin registers through `ctx.shortcuts`, so duplicate or overlapping
bindings are rejected by the harness instead of silently double-firing.
## Why it scales the document root
Most DSH font sizes are hard-coded pixels with no `rem` ladder, so overriding design tokens cannot s
cale the whole interface. `zoom` on `document.documentElement` participates in layout, so the layout
viewport, `position: fixed` menus and overlays, and hit testing all follow — unlike `transform: sca
le()`, which creates a containing block that traps fixed elements.
## Compatibility

- `engines.dsh`: `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`
- Peer: `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `^4.0.1`
- No build step, no
runtime dependencies
## Known limitations
- If you have dragged the conversation width handle, the host stores its own inline width and it win

s over this plugin's compensation; zooming out then scales the column proportionally.
- On Web (a re
al browser tab), `Ctrl+wheel` is the browser's page zoom and cannot be intercepted; use the `Alt` bi

ndings there.
- The plugin scales the document root, so host controls are scaled as well — same as b

.
- The plugin scales the document root, so host controls are scaled as well — same as browser zoom.
